title: Jurassic Park
synopsis: Isla Nublar. A theme park, soft-opening. The fences are electric and the dinosaurs are alive. The power, in two hours, will go off.

nodes.text: You and Ellie arrive. Hammond grins. A brachiosaurus stands beyond the trees.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Joy—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Scientist.

nodes.text: Vials, amber, frogs filling gaps in DNA.

choices.consequence: “Object on principle” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.
“Reserve judgement” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Civil.

nodes.text: Self-driving Jeeps. Lex and Tim in the back.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Care.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Cautious.

nodes.text: The sky opens. A goat is offered. The T. rex does not appear.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Wait” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Brave.

nodes.text: The fences go dark. The T. rex notices. The car splits in half.

nodes.text: Ellie crouches by it, hand on the hide.

nodes.text: Years later you visit a different lab. The science is, again, ahead of the ethics. You decide what to do.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Speak publicly.” The story records the instinct as “Voice” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: Years on, coffee with Ellie. You both still wake at 4 a.m. sometimes.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Action.

Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You and Ellie publish a long paper on de-extinction ethics. It becomes the standard syllabus. You don't, you decide, need to be the regulator. You just need to be the alarm.
You return to paleontology. You discover, in a Montana dig, a fossil that, briefly, shakes the field. You realize the living dinosaurs were, for you, a detour.
Lex becomes a programmer. Tim becomes a paleontologist. They both, separately, send you Christmas cards. The cards are, always, slightly nicer than yours.
